common_name: Sweetheart Passion Fruit (Self-Fertile Purple-Gold Hybrid Passionfruit)

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or grafted plants at the base of a sturdy trellis or fence after the last frost; Sweetheart is an Australian-bred purple x flavicarpa hybrid selected for heavy self-pollinated fruit set without a second vine.

directions: Train onto a strong trellis or fence in full sun and fertile, well-drained soil; Sweetheart was bred in Australia as a cross between purple and golden passionfruit types and is prized by home gardeners because a single vine reliably sets a full crop without a separate pollinator. Fruit is medium-sized with dark reddish-purple skin and the tart-sweet aromatic pulp typical of purple passionfruit, ripening within the first year or two from a rooted cutting. Provide sturdy support and tip-prune regularly, since the vine grows fast and can quickly overwhelm a small trellis if left unchecked. Like other purple-type selections it is more cold-sensitive than Possum Purple, so in zone 9 plant in the warmest, most sheltered spot and mulch heavily before winter.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension -- Passion Fruit Growing in the Home Garden
NSW Department of Primary Industries -- Passionfruit Growing Guide

planting.note: Plant after last frost in full sun on a sturdy trellis; Bruno is one of the original California-grown fuzzy kiwi selections, valued for ripening earlier than Hayward, but it is a female vine and needs a male pollinizer such as Tomuri or Matua planted nearby.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained soil in full sun and train onto a sturdy arbor or T-bar trellis built to carry decades of heavy vine growth. Bruno was one of the earliest fuzzy kiwifruit selections planted commercially in California alongside Hayward, Abbott, Allison, and Monty, and it is distinguished by its narrower, more cylindrical fruit and an earlier harvest window than Hayward. Because kiwi vines are dioecious, a female Bruno vine will not set fruit without a compatible male pollinizer flowering at the same time, and only one male vine is needed to pollinate several females. Prune hard during winter dormancy to control rampant cane growth, thin overcrowded shoots in summer, and expect several years of establishment before the vine reaches full bearing size.
sources: University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources

planting.note: Plant after last frost in full sun on a sturdy trellis; Monty is a productive California fuzzy kiwi selection that ripens later than Hayward, extending the harvest, but it is a female vine and requires a male pollinizer such as Tomuri or Matua nearby.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained soil in full sun and train onto a sturdy arbor or T-bar trellis capable of supporting many years of vigorous growth. Monty was among the original fuzzy kiwifruit cultivars grown commercially in California alongside Hayward, Bruno, Abbott, and Allison, and it is noted for consistent heavy yields and a harvest season that runs later than Hayward, helping spread out the fresh-eating window. As with all fuzzy kiwi, Monty is dioecious and a female vine will not fruit without a compatible male pollinizer blooming nearby at the same time. Prune hard in winter to manage the vine's fast, sprawling growth and to keep fruiting wood accessible, and provide consistent irrigation through the growing season since kiwi vines are shallow-rooted and drought-sensitive.
sources: University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources
